strengths: Forecasting validation loss from partial training is a useful problem for NLP, and the proposed application to hyperparameter selection on the target model is well motivated.

The token-position decomposition yields an interpretable empirical observation. Hyperbolic fits describe position-wise losses across both model sizes and validation distributions, while Appendix Figure 6 provides supporting measurements of actual loss changes.

The experiments include two models trained for 400B tokens, forecasting at multiple observation fractions, ID/OOD validation, and downstream benchmarks. Figure 3 reports promising forecasting accuracy, and the selected data mixtures consistently improve final perplexity in Table 2.
The mathematical pipeline is largely explicit, and the appendix supplies useful architecture, tokenizer, training, package-version, and weighting-strategy details.
weaknesses: The central baseline comparison has a serious unresolved problem. Table 1 reports strongly negative R² for power-law fits evaluated on the complete fitting data. As written, L=(p1*x)^p2+p3 contains a constant predictor when p2=0, so an adequately optimized least-squares fit should achieve R²≥0. These results suggest optimization failure, undocumented constraints, or a reporting problem; they do not establish that power laws cannot describe the trajectory. This comparison needs correction before the claimed superiority is supported.

The experiments do not isolate the benefit of token-position modeling from knowledge of the learning-rate schedule. After a0 and a1 are frozen, Equations 10 and 14 make aggregate predicted loss a shifted cosine. The baselines receive no comparable schedule structure. A direct aggregate-loss predictor using the same piecewise logarithmic/cosine construction is an essential control.

Forecasting generalization is insufficiently established. The functional forms and breakpoint rule are developed using complete trajectories, but no independent discovery/evaluation split across training runs is described. The main experiments also share one architecture family, corpus, context length, training budget, and cosine schedule. OOD validation is useful but does not establish transfer across training regimes. Claims that temporal scaling was previously unexplored also need qualification relative to existing training-step scaling analyses, including Kaplan et al. (2020).

The hyperparameter-selection evidence leaves an important extrapolation gap. Selection uses only 10B of 400B tokens, whereas Figure 3 evaluates forecasting from 40B tokens onward. Predicted versus actual final losses and rankings for all five candidates are missing. The approximately 0.7–1.3% perplexity improvements lack uncertainty estimates, and averaging the last five checkpoints does not establish robustness across independent runs.

Reproducibility remains incomplete despite the appendix. Nonlinear-fitting initialization, parameter constraints, convergence checks, outlier-filtering thresholds, and checkpoint sampling are unspecified. The search candidate count, exact candidate/selected mixtures, and small-model search budget are also absent. No fitting implementation or loss traces are supplied to resolve these ambiguities, which matter particularly given the anomalous baseline results.

The justification for avoiding position-based reweighting overreaches. Equation 17 follows from manually freezing a0 and a1; it is not an independent theoretical result about optimization. Figure 6 supports approximate equality of observed loss decreases, but this does not establish that reweighting cannot help. Three fixed suppression strategies applied after the breakpoint support only a narrow empirical conclusion.

Loss/perplexity reporting needs reconciliation. Substituting Figure 1's parameters into Equation 10 gives approximate ID losses of 1.94 and 1.82, corresponding to perplexities of 6.97 and 6.17. Table 4 instead reports 8.62 and 7.52 for default training under nominally the same setup. Any differences in runs or sequence/domain aggregation should be explained.
